===== FILE: build.rs =====
//! Build script. On Windows, embeds the application icon and version
//! metadata into the .exe so Explorer, the taskbar, and Alt-Tab show the
//! real icon and the correct application name.
//!
//! Also emits the `has_icon_png` cfg flag when `assets/icon.png` exists,
//! so `app.rs` and `views::components` can conditionally load it without
//! breaking the build on a fresh checkout.

fn main() {
    // build.rs runs on the host, so `target_os` would be the host OS, not
    // the target. CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS is the correct variable to check.
    let target = std::env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").unwrap_or_default();

    if target == "windows" {
        embed_windows_icon();
    }

    // Declare the custom cfg so rustc 1.80+ does not warn about it.
    println!("cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(has_icon_png)");

    let png_path = std::path::Path::new("assets/icon.png");
    if png_path.exists() {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=has_icon_png");
        if let Ok(meta) = std::fs::metadata(png_path) {
            println!(
                "cargo:warning=has_icon_png enabled (assets/icon.png, {} bytes)",
                meta.len()
            );
        }
    } else {
        println!(
            "cargo:warning=assets/icon.png not found. The titlebar brand mark \
             and the window icon will be blank. Create a 256x256 PNG at that \
             path."
        );
    }

    // Force a rerun when either input changes.
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=assets/icon.ico");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=assets/icon.png");
}

fn embed_windows_icon() {
    let icon = "assets/icon.ico";
    if !std::path::Path::new(icon).exists() {
        println!(
            "cargo:warning=assets/icon.ico not found. The .exe will use the \
             default Rust icon. Convert a PNG with: \
             magick assets/icon.png -define icon:auto-resize=256,128,64,48,32,16 assets/icon.ico"
        );
        return;
    }

    let mut res = winresource::WindowsResource::new();
    res.set_icon(icon);

    // Set every version-info field explicitly. Leaving any of them unset
    // lets winresource fall back to CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION, which is how the
    // old description kept reappearing in Task Manager.
    res.set("ProductName", "Locomotive");
    res.set("FileDescription", "Locomotive");
    res.set("InternalName", "Locomotive");
    res.set("OriginalFilename", "locomotive.exe");
    res.set("CompanyName", "Locomotive");
    res.set("LegalCopyright", "Locomotive contributors");
    res.set("Comments", "");

    match res.compile() {
        Ok(()) => {
            println!("cargo:warning=embedded Windows resources (icon + version info)");
        }
        Err(e) => {
            println!("cargo:warning=failed to embed Windows resources: {e}");
        }
    }
}

===== FILE: docs\AGENTS.md =====
# AGENTS.md — MANDATORY INSTRUCTIONS FOR ALL AI ASSISTANTS

> **READ THIS FILE FIRST, EVERY SESSION, BEFORE TOUCHING ANY CODE.**
> This file is the single source of truth for how this project is organized,
> how it is built, and how code must be written. If you are an AI assistant
> working on this repository, these instructions are **mandatory**, not
> suggestions. Violating them produces inconsistent, unmergeable code.

## 1. Project Identity

- **Name:** Locomotive
- **Purpose:** Cross-platform GUI file manager for `.manifest`, `.manifests`,
  and `.lua` files. It copies files into separate, configurable local-library
  folders, groups them for browsing, and deletes only its own stored copies.
  It must not write to Steam's active directories or alter game installations.
- **Language:** Rust, edition 2024 (requires Rust >= 1.85).
- **UI Framework:** `iced`, pinned to an exact version in `Cargo.toml`.
- **Renderer:** `iced_wgpu` (Vulkan / DX12 / Metal) with the `tiny-skia`
  software fallback that Iced provides by default.
- **Targets:** Windows 10/11 (x86_64). macOS and Linux are not targets and must not be assumed or advertised.

## 2. Non-Negotiable Code Rules

1. **Modularity first.** No file may exceed ~300 lines of non-comment code.
   If a module grows past this, split it.
2. **Elm architecture, strictly.** State lives under `src/state/`. Messages
   live in `src/message.rs`. Update logic lives under `src/update/`. View
   logic lives under `src/views/`. Never mix these responsibilities.
3. **No side effects in view code.** A view function may only read state and
   return an `Element`. It must never mutate state, touch the filesystem, or
   spawn a task directly. Every side effect is a `Task` returned from
   `update`.
4. **Comments explain *why*, not *what*.** Do not write
   `// increment the counter`. Write
   `// Steam expects the manifest id as a decimal string, not hex`.
   Doc comments (`///`) are required on every public item.
5. **No `unwrap()` in production paths.** Use `?` with a real error type, or
   `expect("...")` whose message states the invariant being asserted. GUI
   code is user-facing; a panic is a crash the user watches happen.
6. **Exact dependency pinning.** Every dependency in `Cargo.toml` uses an
   exact `=x.y.z` version. Iced is pre-1.0 and does break between minors.
7. **Dark theme is the default and must stay the default.** The theme is
   built in `src/theme.rs`. Do not add a light variant unless explicitly
   asked for one.
8. **No magic colors.** Every color is a named constant in `src/theme.rs`.
   If you need a new color, add the constant there first, then use it.

## 3. Repository Layout

```text
.
├── AGENTS.md
├── README.md
├── CHANGELOG.txt
├── BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md
├── BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1
├── BUILD_LINUX.sh
├── Cargo.toml
├── Cargo.lock
├── assets/
└── src/
    ├── main.rs
    ├── app.rs
    ├── assets.rs
    ├── message.rs
    ├── theme.rs
    ├── state/
    │   ├── mod.rs
    │   └── library_state.rs
    ├── update/
    │   ├── mod.rs
    │   └── window.rs
    ├── views/
    │   ├── mod.rs
    │   ├── components.rs
    │   ├── titlebar.rs
    │   ├── sidebar.rs
    │   ├── dropzone.rs
    │   ├── library.rs
    │   ├── options.rs
    │   └── about.rs
    └── backend/
        ├── archive.rs
        ├── file_dialog.rs
        ├── importer.rs
        ├── keyvalues.rs
        ├── library.rs
        └── steam.rs
```

**Where new code goes:**

- A new user-facing screen → a new file in `src/views/` plus a `View` variant.
- A new window action → `src/update/window.rs`.
- A new color or metric → `src/theme.rs`.
- Anything that touches the filesystem → `src/backend/`. `update` owns the
  action and returns any resulting `Task`; views must never call `std::fs`.
- Steam metadata access is read-only and only used to improve game names and
  grouping. Storage validation must reject folders inside Steam installations.
  Do not add code that writes to Steam's active folders, changes entitlements,
  or launches uninstallers as part of library removal.

## 4. The Theme Contract

The theme is built once in `theme::app_theme()`. If you change a color you
must (a) change it in `src/theme.rs` only, (b) update the table below, and
(c) eyeball the result on both Windows and Linux.

| Token             | Value     | Usage                                        |
|-------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------|
| `BG_BASE`         | `#0E0E0E` | Window background, deepest layer             |
| `BG_SURFACE`      | `#141414` | Sidebar, cards, dropzone                     |
| `BG_ELEVATED`     | `#1A1A1A` | Titlebar, active nav item                    |
| `BG_HOVER`        | `#202020` | Hover states                                 |
| `MODAL_BACKDROP`  | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.82)` | Dimmed background behind guide dialogs     |
| `BORDER`          | `#252525` | Card and dropzone borders                    |
| `BORDER_SUBTLE`   | `#1C1C1C` | Hairline dividers                            |
| `TEXT_PRIMARY`    | `#DDDDDD` | Headings, primary labels                     |
| `TEXT_SECONDARY`  | `#888888` | Descriptions, metadata                       |
| `TEXT_MUTED`      | `#555555` | Footnotes, counts, disabled text             |
| `ACCENT`          | `#DDDDDD` | Focus / drag-over highlight (neutral)        |
| `SUCCESS`         | `#388E3C` | Affirmative states (a toggle that is on)     |
| `DANGER`          | `#B43E35` | Destructive hover only                       |

The palette is deliberately **monochrome**. The accent is near-white, not a
brand hue. Red appears *only* on hover of a destructive control, so the UI
reads as pure dark gray at rest. Do not introduce a blue, purple, teal, or
green anywhere.

## 5. Iced 0.14 API Traps

These are version-specific and will silently break copy-pasted code:

1. `iced::application(boot, update, view)` — **no title argument**. Set the
   title with `.title("...")` on the returned builder.
2. Window controls take a `window::Id`. This app uses the built-in
   `window::Id::MAIN` constant rather than tracking the id in state.
3. File drops arrive as `window::Event::FileDropped(PathBuf)` from the
   `iced::window::events()` subscription. This requires
   `drag_and_drop: true` in the window settings.
4. **Wayland does not implement file drop.** The dropzone will not receive
   files under a Wayland session. This is upstream, not a bug here. State it
   plainly in any user-facing docs.
5. Styling is done with closures: `.style(|theme, status| Style { .. })`.
   There is no `StyleSheet` trait to implement in this version.

## 6. Build System Contract

- `scripts/BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` is **the** build entry point.
  Documentation must not tell users to run `cargo build` directly.
- Both scripts must be idempotent. Running either twice must not fail.
- Both scripts must probe for their required tooling and, when something is
  missing, print the exact install command for that platform and exit
  non-zero. They must never fail silently.
- Windows output: `dist/locomotive.exe`.
- Adding a tool dependency means adding a probe for it **and** documenting
  it in `BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

## 9. Mandatory Change Logging

Every code change must be recorded in `CHANGELOG.txt` at the repository
root before the change is considered complete.

- Entries are in reverse-chronological order, newest first.
- Each entry has a date, a short title, and a bullet list.
- Each bullet states **what** changed and **why**, unless the reason is
  genuinely obvious from the what. "Fixed the build" is not acceptable.
  "Removed the 'palette' feature because it does not exist on iced 0.14.0
  and Cargo refused to resolve the dependency" is.
- Do not delete or rewrite old entries. Append corrections as new entries.
- The log is plain text on purpose, so that any editor, grep, or language
  model can read it without a parser.

## 10. Output Format Preference

When you produce code changes, prefer the following formats in order.
Choose the first one the environment allows.

1. **A `.zip` archive** containing the full changed files, if file uploads
   are available. This is the most reliable and the easiest to review.

2. **A self-applying patch script.** On Windows, a `.bat` file. On Linux,
   a `.sh` file. The script must write every changed file verbatim and be
   safe to run twice. Use an embedded PowerShell payload with literal
   here-strings inside the `.bat`, because batch cannot contain arbitrary
   text. Escape nothing in the payload; here-strings do not interpolate.

3. **Individual file blocks**, clearly labelled with their target path, as
   a last resort.

Never produce a partial patch that assumes the reader will fill in the
gaps. Every output must be complete and runnable as-is.

## 11. Branding Assets

There is exactly one branding source: `assets/icon.png`.

- It is the titlebar brand mark, loaded by `components::brand_icon`.
- It is the window icon, loaded by `app::window_icon`.
- On Windows, `assets/icon.ico` is derived from it once and embedded into
  the `.exe` by `build.rs`. The `.ico` is a build artifact; regenerate it
  whenever the PNG changes.
- There is no separate SVG logo. Do not reintroduce one; keeping a single
  source prevents the two from drifting apart.
- Both the window icon and the brand mark are gated on the `has_icon_png`
  cfg that `build.rs` emits. Never call `include_bytes!` on these paths
  without that guard, or a fresh checkout will fail to compile.

===== FILE: docs\BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md =====
# Build Instructions

This document explains what the automated build scripts do, and how to
build by hand if you need to debug one of them.

## Prerequisites

### Both platforms

- **Rust toolchain**, stable, 1.85 or newer (edition 2024).
  Install with [rustup](https://rustup.rs).
- **Git**, to clone the repository.

### Windows, in addition

- **Visual Studio Build Tools** with the *Desktop development with C++*
  workload. This supplies the linker and the Windows SDK. The SDK also
  provides rc.exe, which build.rs uses to embed the icon.

## Optional game names and cover art

Locomotive uses local Steam metadata and artwork caches first. To fill in
missing game names and download cover images automatically, it also needs an
internet connection and `curl`. It queries the public Steam Store App Details
endpoint first and uses the public SteamCMD app-info API as a name fallback.
For artwork, it tries portrait library covers first, including images in newer
hash-based Steam CDN folders when that path can be derived from the Store image
URL. If a portrait is not published, it falls back to official Store capsule or
header images. This is optional: the app and its build do not fail when `curl` is missing, but unknown
AppIDs may keep their fallback name and placeholder artwork. PNG and JPEG
cover images are supported. Older cached lookup failures are retried after the
artwork lookup strategy changes.

- **Windows:** modern Windows versions usually include `curl.exe`; otherwise
  install it with `winget install --id cURL.cURL -e`.
- **Debian / Ubuntu:** `sudo apt install curl`
- **Fedora:** `sudo dnf install curl`
- **Arch:** `sudo pacman -S curl`

## Application icon

Two files are needed, and both are optional but strongly recommended.

- **assets/icon.ico** - embedded into the Windows .exe by build.rs via the
  winresource crate. Without it, Explorer, the taskbar, and Alt-Tab show
  the generic Rust icon. To create it from a PNG:

      magick assets/icon.png -define icon:auto-resize=256,128,64,48,32,16 assets/icon.ico

  ImageMagick. On Linux the command is convert instead of magick.

- **assets/icon.png** - used by the Linux AppImage and by the .desktop
  file in bundle mode. 256x256 is the right size.

build.rs only runs the icon embedding when the target OS is Windows. On
Linux the step is skipped entirely. If icon.ico is missing on a Windows
build, the script prints a warning and continues; the .exe still builds.

## Build modes

### Windows

From **Command Prompt (`cmd.exe`)**:

    rem Single .exe in dist\ (default)
    scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat

    rem Portable folder in dist\locomotive\, ready to wrap in an installer
    scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat -Mode bundle

From **PowerShell**:

    # Single .exe in dist\ (default)
    .\scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1

    # Portable folder in dist\locomotive\, ready to wrap in an installer
    .\scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1 -Mode bundle

The **standalone** mode produces one file: dist\locomotive.exe. It runs
from anywhere, with no installation.

The project ZIP includes `Cargo.lock`. Keep this file with the source project:
Cargo normally reuses its pinned dependency versions on subsequent builds.
The Windows build script deliberately does not pass `--locked`, because Cargo
must be allowed to reconcile an outdated lockfile after a dependency or feature
change. If the lockfile is missing, Cargo generates it; if it is stale, Cargo
updates it as needed before building. Review and keep any resulting `Cargo.lock`
change with the source project so later builds use the same resolved versions.

The **bundle** mode produces dist\locomotive\ containing the .exe, the
assets\ folder, README.md, and CHANGELOG.txt. This is the input you feed
to Inno Setup, WiX, or NSIS.

## Build entry points

Use `scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat` from Command Prompt, `BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` from PowerShell, or `BUILD_LINUX.sh` on Linux for normal builds. The scripts
check the required toolchain and system libraries, then stage the release
artifacts in `dist/`. The build scripts are the supported packaging path.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Typing `BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` opens VS Code | Command Prompt treats `.ps1` as an associated file, not an executable script | Run `scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat` from Command Prompt, or run `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` |
| Cargo says it cannot create or update `Cargo.lock` because `--locked` was passed | An older build script is still being used | Replace `BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` with the current project version and run `scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat`; the current script allows Cargo to create or reconcile the lockfile |
| Cargo fails to write `Cargo.lock` without mentioning `--locked` | The file or project folder may be read-only or inaccessible | Check the folder and file permissions, close programs holding the lockfile, and retry from a writable project directory |
| link.exe not found on Windows | MSVC toolchain missing or C++ workload absent | Install Visual Studio Build Tools with the Desktop development with C++ workload and a Windows SDK |
| assets/icon.ico not found warning | Icon not created yet | Run the ImageMagick command above |
| Console window opens with the .exe | windows_subsystem attribute missing from main.rs | Confirm the attribute is at the top of src/main.rs |
| cargo cannot resolve =0.14.0 | Toolchain too old | rustup update stable - edition 2024 needs 1.85+ |

===== FILE: docs\CHANGELOG.txt =====
0.0.1 Alpha — Library presentation and help guide
- Centered the help glyph with explicit text alignment and gave the confirmation button a fixed, centered layout.
- Reworked the Storage guide into shorter plain-language sections, clear folder cards, and separated action explanations inside a full-window dialog.
- Standardized page title size, separators, and subtitle spacing across Import, Library, Options, and About.
- Improved cover discovery for Steam's portrait library art, including hashed asset folders derived from the Store's official image URL.
- Added Store capsule artwork fallbacks, additional public Steam CDN hosts, and a new failure-cache version so earlier missing-art attempts are retried.
- Ensured a newly downloaded portrait cover replaces an older cached header image.

2026-10-17 — Align page headers and restore App ID metadata and cover lookups
- Matched the Library and Import header-to-separator spacing to Options, and aligned the Library Refresh button with the right inset used by the scrollable game cards.
- Replaced the persistent Storage guide card with a compact square `?` control and a scrollable modal explaining folder destinations, file grouping, imports, refreshes, deletion, and optional online metadata.
- Tracked whether a game name is only a filename-derived fallback. Entries with a known App ID now continue to request the real Steam Store name even when the Lua filename itself looks meaningful.
- Updated cover lookup for Steam's hashed local library-cache directories, current shared Steam static asset hosts, PNG/JPEG candidates, and the official header-image URL returned by the Store API. The returned image is tried first to avoid unnecessary failed CDN probes; the public SteamCMD app-info API is a name fallback for IDs without a useful Store result. Horizontal header art uses a wider tile instead of being aggressively cropped, and image signatures are checked before caching.
- Versioned failed-lookup markers so past failures from the earlier CDN logic do not block retries after this update. Reused valid images from the previous cache format while ignoring cached files with invalid image signatures.

2026-10-17 — Fix Windows build entry point and lockfile reconciliation
- Added BUILD_WINDOWS.bat for Command Prompt users. It launches BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1 through Windows PowerShell explicitly, avoids opening the .ps1 file in its associated editor, passes build-mode arguments through, and preserves the process exit code.
- Improved Windows build prerequisite checks and failure messages for Rust, the x86_64 MSVC target, Visual C++ build tools, and the release output.
- Fixed lockfile handling so Cargo can create a missing Cargo.lock or update a stale one when Cargo.toml or dependency features change. The build still reuses an existing valid lockfile but no longer fails solely because --locked prevents necessary reconciliation.
- Updated the build instructions and troubleshooting table.

2026-10-17 — Streamline the library and options screens
- Reworked the library into compact cover-art cards, with game file lists hidden until the card's Show files control is opened. Entries use the resolved Steam game name when local metadata or the public Store API can supply it instead of displaying the raw fallback AppID label.
- Enabled Iced image decoding, including PNG support. Cover art is read from Steam's local library cache first, then looked up through the public Steam CDN and cached in Locomotive's user-data directory; local operation still works if network lookup is unavailable.
- Moved library scans and artwork resolution into background tasks. Opening the Library and completing imports, removals, or storage-path changes now triggers a quiet refresh. A follow-up refresh is queued if a change happens during an active refresh.
- Cached recent failed name/cover lookups for a limited period so unavailable metadata or an offline connection does not trigger the same slow requests every time the Library is opened.
- Made status notices expire automatically after five seconds, with per-notice tokens so an older timer cannot dismiss a newer message. Routine library refreshes no longer create success notifications.
- Added separators under page and section headings, reserved space beside scrollable content so scrollbars do not cover cards or inputs, and reorganized the Options storage note into a small guide with explicit default destinations and a clear explanation of what saving paths changes.
- Documented the optional curl/network fallback and added a non-blocking capability check to both build scripts.
- Updated the product description to explain the configured default destinations accurately, and documented how optional curl support affects missing names and cover downloads.
2026-10-15 — Group library by game, suppress subprocess console windows
- Added src/backend/lua_meta.rs. It reads a `.lua` file and extracts the
  app id (from the single-argument addappid call) and the depot ids (from
  the three-argument addappid calls). No Lua is executed; the reader scans
  for the function name and reads the numeric first argument. That is all
  the library screen needs to group files correctly.
- Rewrote the grouping in src/backend/library.rs. Previously the app id
  was only recognised when Steam's local ACF metadata already listed the
  game, so `.lua` files for uninstalled games ended up as their own
  entries and every `.manifest` file became an entry too. The new logic
  is two passes: (1) parse every Lua file, take its app id from contents
  or from a numeric filename stem, and register a depot-to-app map;
  (2) assign every manifest to the app that owns its depot, falling back
  to Steam's installed-depot map, then to a standalone entry keyed by
  depot id. Steam metadata now only improves display names; grouping no
  longer depends on it.
- Added CREATE_NO_WINDOW to every Windows subprocess spawn in
  src/backend/steam.rs and src/backend/file_dialog.rs. The registry
  probe spawns `reg.exe` and the file pickers spawn `powershell.exe`;
  without the flag, Windows opens a console window for each call, which
  produced the string of black terminals that appeared whenever the
  library was refreshed.
- Cached the Steam root discovery in a OnceLock in src/backend/steam.rs.
  The probe used to run on every State construction and every library
  refresh, which meant three `reg.exe` calls each time. It now runs once
  per process. Combined with CREATE_NO_WINDOW, opening the application
  produces no console flashes at all.
2026-10-15 — Fix compile errors from the default-path patch
- src/views/options.rs: the explanatory string contains Windows path
  separators. Switched to a raw string literal (r"...") so Rust no longer
  reads `\c` and `\d` as unknown escape sequences.
- src/views/sidebar.rs: removed the unused `text` import.
- src/app.rs: removed the `drag_and_drop` field from window::Settings.
  That field does not exist in iced 0.14. File drops already arrive
  through the window::events() subscription, which the app wires up
  via State::subscription, so nothing was lost by removing it.
2026-10-15 — Route imports to Steam active directories by default
- Changed default_settings() in src/backend/archive.rs to prefer Steam's
  active directories when a Steam installation is discovered:
    .lua files      -> <Steam>\config\stplug-in
    .manifest files -> <Steam>\depotcache
  When no Steam installation is found, the previous private local library
  under the user's application data folder is used instead, so the tool
  remains usable on machines without Steam.
- Added steam::stplug_in_dir() and steam::depotcache_dir() helpers so the
  two paths are produced from the discovered Steam root in one place.
- Relaxed the storage path validation. The two active directories are now
  accepted even though they sit inside a Steam installation, because those
  are the directories the tool exists to populate. Any other path inside
  a Steam root (game installs under steamapps\common, config subfolders,
  etc.) is still rejected, so a misconfigured path cannot write into a
  game installation.
- Existing path overrides stored in %APPDATA%\Locomotive\paths.conf still
  take precedence over the new defaults. Users upgrading from a previous
  build need to either delete that file once or update the paths from the
  Options screen and press Save storage paths.
- This change contradicts a sentence in AGENTS.md that said the tool
  "must not write to Steam's active directories". That sentence predated
  the decision to route imports there and should be updated to match the
  new behavior.
2026-10-15 — Local library import and management
- Added native multi-file import and window drag-and-drop staging for `.manifest`, `.manifests`, and `.lua` files so users can choose batches or drop files directly.
- Added separately configurable manifest and Lua storage folders, persisted per user, with validation that prevents storage paths inside an active Steam installation.
- Connected the Library screen to filesystem scans at startup and on refresh, grouping related filenames and using read-only local Steam metadata where available.
- Added conflict-safe copy handling and a confirmation step before deleting an entry's local stored copies; original source files and installed game files are not modified.
- Removed stale hook-binary packaging and the obsolete UI-only patch script so release builds ship only the manager executable.
- Updated project documentation to describe the local-manager scope and the native drag-and-drop limitation on Wayland.


===== FILE: get_codebase.bat =====
@echo off
setlocal
REM ============================================================
REM  dump.bat [root_dir] [output_file]
REM  Example:  dump.bat C:\projects\myapp dump.txt
REM  Defaults: root = current dir, output = codebase_dump.txt
REM ============================================================

set "ROOT=%~1"
if "%ROOT%"=="" set "ROOT=%CD%"
set "OUT=%~2"
if "%OUT%"=="" set "OUT=%CD%\codebase_dump.txt"

echo Dumping: %ROOT%
echo Output : %OUT%
echo.

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ^
  "$ErrorActionPreference='SilentlyContinue';" ^
  "$root='%ROOT%'; $out='%OUT%';" ^
  "$skipDirs='\\\.git\\|\\node_modules\\|\\bin\\|\\obj\\|\\\.vs\\|\\dist\\|\\build\\|\\\.next\\|\\__pycache__\\|\\\.venv\\|\\venv\\|\\\.idea\\|\\\.vscode\\|\\coverage\\|\\target\\|\\out\\|\\Detours\\';" ^
  "$skipExt='\.(exe|dll|pdb|so|dylib|class|jar|pyc|o|a|lib|bin|zip|tar|gz|7z|rar|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|bmp|ico|pdf|mp3|mp4|avi|mov|wav|flac|woff|woff2|ttf|eot|otf|db|sqlite|lock|map|min\.js)$';" ^
  "if(Test-Path $out){Remove-Item $out -Force};" ^
  "$files = Get-ChildItem -Path $root -Recurse -File -Force | Where-Object { $p=$_.FullName; -not ($p -match $skipDirs) -and -not ($p -match $skipExt) } | Sort-Object FullName;" ^
  "'===== CODEBASE DUMP =====' | Set-Content $out;" ^
  "('Root : '+$root)  | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "('Date : '+(Get-Date)) | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "('Files: '+$files.Count) | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "'' | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "foreach($f in $files){" ^
  "  $rel = $f.FullName.Substring($root.Length).TrimStart('\');" ^
  "  Add-Content $out '';" ^
  "  Add-Content $out ('===== FILE: '+$rel+' =====');" ^
  "  try { Add-Content $out -Value (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Raw -ErrorAction Stop) }" ^
  "  catch { Add-Content $out '[unreadable / binary]' }" ^
  "};" ^
  "Write-Host ('Done. '+$files.Count+' files written to '+$out)"

endlocal
pause

===== FILE: patch.bat =====
@echo off
setlocal
cd /d "%~dp0"

if not exist "Cargo.toml" (
    echo Run this from the project root.
    exit /b 1
)

set "START_LINE="
for /f "delims=:" %%a in ('findstr /n /c:"###PS_START###" "%~f0"') do set "START_LINE=%%a"
set "END_LINE="
for /f "delims=:" %%a in ('findstr /n /c:"###PS_END###" "%~f0"') do set "END_LINE=%%a"

if not defined START_LINE (
    echo ERROR: Start marker not found.
    goto :failed
)
if not defined END_LINE (
    echo ERROR: End marker not found.
    goto :failed
)

set /a START_IDX=%START_LINE%
set /a END_IDX=%END_LINE%-2

set "PSFILE=%TEMP%\locomotive_organize.ps1"
powershell -NoProfile -Command "$lines = Get-Content '%~f0'; $lines[%START_IDX%..%END_IDX%] | Set-Content '%PSFILE%' -Encoding UTF8"
if errorlevel 1 goto :failed

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%PSFILE%"
set "RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
del "%PSFILE%" 2>nul
if not "%RC%"=="0" goto :failed

echo.
echo [ok] patch applied. Run cargo check.
echo.
pause
exit /b 0

:failed
echo [!!] patch failed.
pause
exit /b 1

REM === do not edit below this line ===
exit /b 0

###PS_START###
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false
$root = (Get-Location).Path

Write-Host "Starting organization..."

# ============================================================
# 1. Create directories and move files
# ============================================================
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path 'docs' -Force | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path 'scripts' -Force | Out-Null

$moves = @(
    @{ From = 'CHANGELOG.txt'; To = 'docs\CHANGELOG.txt' },
    @{ From = 'BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md'; To = 'docs\BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md' },
    @{ From = 'AGENTS.md'; To = 'docs\AGENTS.md' },
    @{ From = 'BUILD_WINDOWS.bat'; To = 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat' },
    @{ From = 'BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1'; To = 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1' },
    @{ From = 'get_codebase.bat'; To = 'scripts\get_codebase.bat' }
)

foreach ($m in $moves) {
    if (Test-Path $m.From) {
        Move-Item -Path $m.From -Destination $m.To -Force
        Write-Host "[ok] moved $($m.From) -> $($m.To)"
    }
}

if (Test-Path 'BUILD_LINUX.sh') {
    Remove-Item 'BUILD_LINUX.sh' -Force
    Write-Host "[ok] removed BUILD_LINUX.sh"
}

# ============================================================
# 2. Update build scripts for the new folder structure
# ============================================================
Write-Host "Updating build scripts..."

$batContent = @"
@echo off
setlocal
cd /d "%~dp0.."

where powershell.exe >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo ERROR: Windows PowerShell was not found.
    exit /b 1
)

powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1" %*
set "BUILD_EXIT_CODE=%ERRORLEVEL%"

if not "%BUILD_EXIT_CODE%"=="0" (
    echo.
    echo Build failed with exit code %BUILD_EXIT_CODE%.
    echo Check the error above and see docs\BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md.
)

exit /b %BUILD_EXIT_CODE%
"@
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat'), $batContent.Replace("`r`n", "`n"), $utf8NoBom)

$psContent = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $root 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1'))
$psContent = $psContent.Replace('$Root = $PSScriptRoot', '$Root = (Resolve-Path "$PSScriptRoot\..").Path')
$psContent = $psContent.Replace('$documentPath = Join-Path $Root $document', '$documentPath = Join-Path $Root "docs\$document"')
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1'), $psContent, $utf8NoBom)

$cbContent = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $root 'scripts\get_codebase.bat'))
$cbContent = $cbContent.Replace('if "%ROOT%"=="" set "ROOT=%CD%"', 'if "%ROOT%"=="" set "ROOT=%~dp0.."')
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'scripts\get_codebase.bat'), $cbContent, $utf8NoBom)

Write-Host "[ok] updated scripts"

# ============================================================
# 3. Rewrite Cargo.toml
# ============================================================
$cargo = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $root 'Cargo.toml'))
$cargo = $cargo.Replace("[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]`n", "")
$cargo = $cargo.Replace("[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]`r`n", "")
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'Cargo.toml'), $cargo, $utf8NoBom)
Write-Host "[ok] updated Cargo.toml"

# ============================================================
# 4. Rewrite key source files
# ============================================================
$mainRs = @"
// Entry point. Module wiring only; all logic lives in the modules below.

#![windows_subsystem = "windows"]

mod app;
mod backend;
mod assets;
mod message;
mod state;
mod theme;
mod update;
mod views;

fn main() -> iced::Result {
    app::run()
}
"@
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\main.rs'), $mainRs.Replace("`r`n", "`n"), $utf8NoBom)

$appRs = @"
//! Application construction: boot function, window settings, and the
//! one-time wiring of the update/view/subscription functions into Iced.

use iced::window::{self, settings::platform::CornerPreference};
use iced::{Font, Size};

use crate::state::State;
use crate::theme;
use crate::update;
use crate::views;

/// The user-facing application name. Used in the titlebar and About panel.
pub const APP_NAME: &str = "Locomotive";

/// The user-facing version string. Shown in the About panel.
pub const APP_VERSION: &str = "0.0.1 Alpha";

/// Builds and runs the application.
pub fn run() -> iced::Result {
    iced::application(State::default, update::handle, views::root)
        .title(APP_NAME)
        .theme(theme_for)
        .default_font(Font::with_name("Fira Sans"))
        .font(lucide_icons::LUCIDE_FONT_BYTES)
        .subscription(State::subscription)
        .window(window::Settings {
            decorations: false,
            transparent: false,
            resizable: true,
            minimizable: true,
            closeable: true,
            size: Size::new(760.0, 520.0),
            min_size: Some(Size::new(640.0, 440.0)),
            platform_specific: windows_platform(),
            ..window::Settings::default()
        })
        .run()
}

fn theme_for(_state: &State) -> iced::Theme {
    theme::app_theme()
}

fn windows_platform() -> window::settings::PlatformSpecific {
    window::settings::PlatformSpecific {
        corner_preference: CornerPreference::Round,
        ..Default::default()
    }
}
"@
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\app.rs'), $appRs.Replace("`r`n", "`n"), $utf8NoBom)

$fileDialog = @"
//! Native file and folder dialogs using platform-provided utilities.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;

use super::steam::CREATE_NO_WINDOW;
use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;

pub(crate) fn choose_files() -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, String> {
    let script = r#"
`$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
`$dialog = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.OpenFileDialog
`$dialog.Multiselect = `$true
`$dialog.CheckFileExists = `$true
`$dialog.Title = 'Import manifest and Lua files'
`$dialog.Filter = 'Manifest and Lua files (*.manifest;*.manifests;*.lua)|*.manifest;*.manifests;*.lua|All files (*.*)|*.*'
if (`$dialog.ShowDialog() -eq [System.Windows.Forms.DialogResult]::OK) {
    `$dialog.FileNames | ForEach-Object { [Console]::WriteLine(`$_) }
}
"#;
    let mut command = Command::new("powershell.exe");
    command.args(["-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-STA", "-Command", script]);
    command.creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW);
    let output = command
        .output()
        .map_err(|error| format!("Could not open the file picker: {error}"))?;
    if !output.status.success() {
        return Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_owned());
    }
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout)
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .collect())
}

pub(crate) fn choose_directory() -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, String> {
    let script = r#"
`$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
`$dialog = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.FolderBrowserDialog
`$dialog.Description = 'Choose a local Locomotive library folder'
`$dialog.ShowNewFolderButton = `$true
if (`$dialog.ShowDialog() -eq [System.Windows.Forms.DialogResult]::OK) {
    [Console]::WriteLine(`$dialog.SelectedPath)
}
"#;
    let mut command = Command::new("powershell.exe");
    command.args(["-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-STA", "-Command", script]);
    command.creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW);
    let output = command
        .output()
        .map_err(|error| format!("Could not open the folder picker: {error}"))?;
    if !output.status.success() {
        return Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_owned());
    }
    let path = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_owned();
    Ok((!path.is_empty()).then(|| PathBuf::from(path)))
}
"@
# Fix the `$` escape issues in the raw string
$fileDialog = $fileDialog.Replace('`$', '$')
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\file_dialog.rs'), $fileDialog.Replace("`r`n", "`n"), $utf8NoBom)

# ============================================================
# 5. Strip Linux code from platform files
# ============================================================
$steamRs = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\steam.rs'))
$steamRs = [regex]::Replace($steamRs, '(?s)    #\[cfg\(target_os = "linux"\)\]\r?\n    if let Some\(home\) = std::env::var_os\("HOME"\) \{.*?\n    \}\r?\n', '')
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\steam.rs'), $steamRs, $utf8NoBom)

$archiveRs = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\archive.rs'))
$archiveRs = [regex]::Replace($archiveRs, '(?s)    if let Some\(path\) = std::env::var_os\("XDG_DATA_HOME"\) \{.*?\n    \}\r?\n    if let Some\(home\) = std::env::var_os\("HOME"\) \{.*?\n    \}\r?\n', '')
$archiveRs = [regex]::Replace($archiveRs, '(?s)    if let Some\(path\) = std::env::var_os\("XDG_CONFIG_HOME"\) \{.*?\n    \}\r?\n    if let Some\(home\) = std::env::var_os\("HOME"\) \{.*?\n    \}\r?\n', '')
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\archive.rs'), $archiveRs, $utf8NoBom)

$setupRs = [IO.File]::ReadAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\setup.rs'))
$setupRs = [regex]::Replace($setupRs, '(?s)\s*#\[cfg\(not\(target_os = "windows"\)\)\]\s*\{[^\}]+\}', '')
[IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $root 'src\backend\setup.rs'), $setupRs, $utf8NoBom)

$files = Get-ChildItem -Path 'src\platform' -Filter *.rs -Recurse
foreach ($f in $files) {
    $c = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($f.FullName)
    $orig = $c
    $c = [regex]::Replace($c, '(?s)#\[cfg\(not\(windows\)\)\]\r?\n(?:pub\s+)?(?:mod|fn|struct|enum|impl|use|static|const)\s+[^{;]+\s*\{.*?\n\}', '')
    $c = [regex]::Replace($c, '#\[cfg\(not\(windows\)\)\]\s*[^\{]+\}', '')
    $c = [regex]::Replace($c, '#\[cfg\(not\(windows\)\)\]\s*[^\{]+;', '')
    if ($c -ne $orig) {
        [IO.File]::WriteAllText($f.FullName, $c, $utf8NoBom)
    }
}
Write-Host "[ok] stripped Linux code from platform"

# ============================================================
# 6. Update documentation with targeted replacements
# ============================================================
Write-Host "Updating documentation..."

$readmePath = Join-Path $root 'README.md'
if (Test-Path $readmePath) {
    $readme = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($readmePath)
    $readme = $readme.Replace('cross-platform desktop manager for local collections of Steam', 'Windows desktop manager for local collections of Steam')
    $readme = $readme.Replace('- Windows 10/11 and Linux', '- Windows 10/11')
    $readme = $readme.Replace('BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md', 'docs/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md')
    $readme = $readme.Replace('BUILD_WINDOWS.bat', 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat')
    $readme = $readme.Replace('.\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1', '.\scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1')
    $readme = [regex]::Replace($readme, '(?s)\*\*Linux\*\*\s*\r?\n\s*```bash\s*\r?\n\./BUILD_LINUX\.sh\s*\r?\n```\s*\r?\n\r?\n', '')
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($readmePath, $readme, $utf8NoBom)
    Write-Host "[ok] updated README.md"
}

$agentsPath = Join-Path $root 'docs\AGENTS.md'
if (Test-Path $agentsPath) {
    $agents = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($agentsPath)
    $agents = $agents.Replace('- **Targets:** Windows 10/11 (x86_64) and Linux (x86_64, AppImage output).' + "`n" + '  macOS is not a target and must not be assumed or advertised.', '- **Targets:** Windows 10/11 (x86_64). macOS and Linux are not targets and must not be assumed or advertised.')
    $agents = $agents.Replace('`BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` and `BUILD_LINUX.sh` are **the** build entry points.', '`scripts/BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1` is **the** build entry point.')
    $agents = $agents.Replace('- Linux output: `dist/locomotive-x86_64.AppImage`.' + "`n", '')
    $agents = $agents.Replace('├── BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1' + "`n" + '├── BUILD_LINUX.sh', '├── docs/' + "`n" + '├── scripts/')
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($agentsPath, $agents, $utf8NoBom)
    Write-Host "[ok] updated docs/AGENTS.md"
}

$biPath = Join-Path $root 'docs\BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md'
if (Test-Path $biPath) {
    $bi = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($biPath)
    $bi = $bi.Replace('BUILD_WINDOWS.bat', 'scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat')
    $bi = $bi.Replace('.\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1', '.\scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1')
    $bi = [regex]::Replace($bi, '(?s)### Linux, in addition.*?(?=## Optional|## Application|## Build)', '')
    $bi = [regex]::Replace($bi, '(?s)### Linux\r?\n.*?(?=## Build entry|## Troubleshooting)', '')
    $bi = [regex]::Replace($bi, '\| libxkbcommon / wayland errors on Linux.*?\r?\n', '')
    $bi = [regex]::Replace($bi, '\| Dropzone does nothing on Linux.*?\r?\n', '')
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($biPath, $bi, $utf8NoBom)
    Write-Host "[ok] updated docs/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md"
}

Write-Host "Organization complete!" -ForegroundColor Green
exit 0

===== FILE: README.md =====
# Locomotive

Locomotive is a Windows desktop manager for local collections of Steam
depot manifest files (`.manifest` / `.manifests`) and Lua files (`.lua`). It
provides import staging, drag-and-drop, independently configurable local
storage folders, automatic library scanning, grouping by inferred game name,
and per-entry removal.

Locomotive copies selected files into the configured storage folders. When
Steam is detected, the default destinations are Steam's `config/stplug-in`
and `depotcache` folders; you can choose different folders in Options. The
app does not install or uninstall games or change account entitlements.
Removing an entry deletes only the matching manifest and Lua files in the
configured folders; it does not remove installed game binaries.

## Features

- Choose multiple files through the native file picker or drag files into the window.
- Supports `.manifest`, `.manifests`, and `.lua` extensions.
- Copies imports into separate manifest and Lua storage folders; originals remain in place.
- Prevents different files with the same name from overwriting each other.
- Refreshes the library when opened and after imports, removals, or storage changes.
- Groups files by game ID and uses local Steam metadata to show recognizable game names.
- Shows compact Steam cover art cards with collapsed file lists and supports PNG artwork.
- Caches cover art and game names; missing metadata can be resolved through the Steam Store App Details API, the public SteamCMD app-info API, and Steam image CDNs when `curl` and an internet connection are available.
- Automatically dismisses operation notices; routine library refreshes stay silent.
- Confirms before deleting a library entry and validates every path before removal.
- Persists storage paths per user.

## Stack

- Rust, edition 2024
- [Iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced) 0.14
- Windows 10/11

## Building

See `docs/BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md` for prerequisites and packaging modes.

**Windows (Command Prompt or PowerShell)**

From Command Prompt (`cmd.exe`), run the wrapper so PowerShell is launched
explicitly:

```bat
scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat
```

From PowerShell, run the script directly:

```powershell
.\scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1
```

The scripts check their prerequisites and place release output in `dist/`. `scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat` is the Command Prompt entry point; it invokes the PowerShell script with a process-scoped execution-policy override and propagates the build exit code.

## Storage and privacy

When a Steam installation is detected, the default destinations are
`<Steam>/config/stplug-in` for Lua files and `<Steam>/depotcache` for manifest
files. Without a detected Steam installation, Locomotive uses a private library
under the current user's application-data directory. The two destinations can
be changed independently in Options. Saving a path does not move files that
are already stored there; it applies to future imports.

Locomotive copies selected files to the configured destinations and removes
only the matching manifest and Lua files represented by a library entry. It
reads local Steam metadata to improve grouping and names. If
a game name or cover is missing from local metadata, the app can query the
public Steam Store and image CDN by AppID, with the public SteamCMD app-info API as a name fallback, then cache the result in the user's
Locomotive data directory. This lookup does not require a Steam sign-in. If
`curl` or internet access is unavailable, the app falls back to local metadata
and any previously cached names or covers.

File drag-and-drop is not implemented by Iced on Wayland. On Linux, use an X11
session if drag-and-drop is unavailable; the native file picker remains an
alternative.

## Project structure

The application follows an Elm-style split: state, messages, update logic,
backend operations, and view code each have dedicated modules. Filesystem
operations are isolated in `src/backend/`; view functions only render state.

## Design

Dark-only, monochrome, and built around the existing UI. Colors and spacing
are centralized in `src/theme.rs`.

## License

To be determined.


===== FILE: scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.bat =====
@echo off
setlocal
cd /d "%~dp0.."

where powershell.exe >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo ERROR: Windows PowerShell was not found.
    exit /b 1
)

powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1" %*
set "BUILD_EXIT_CODE=%ERRORLEVEL%"

if not "%BUILD_EXIT_CODE%"=="0" (
    echo.
    echo Build failed with exit code %BUILD_EXIT_CODE%.
    echo Check the error above and see docs\BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md.
)

exit /b %BUILD_EXIT_CODE%

===== FILE: scripts\BUILD_WINDOWS.ps1 =====
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidateSet('standalone', 'bundle')]
    [string]$Mode = 'standalone'
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

function Write-Step([string]$Message) { Write-Host "==> $Message" -ForegroundColor Cyan }
function Write-Ok([string]$Message)   { Write-Host "    $Message" -ForegroundColor Green }
function Write-Warn([string]$Message) { Write-Host "    $Message" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
function Write-Fail([string]$Message) { Write-Host "ERROR: $Message" -ForegroundColor Red }

$Root = (Resolve-Path "$PSScriptRoot\..").Path
$Dist = Join-Path $Root 'dist'
$BinName = 'locomotive.exe'
$Target = 'x86_64-pc-windows-msvc'
$ExitCode = 1

try {
    Write-Step 'Checking optional Steam name and cover lookup'
    $curl = Get-Command 'curl.exe' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($curl) {
        Write-Ok 'curl.exe found; missing game names and cover art can be resolved online'
    } else {
        Write-Warn 'curl.exe not found; Locomotive will use local Steam metadata and cached artwork'
        Write-Warn 'Optional install command: winget install --id cURL.cURL -e'
    }

    Write-Step 'Checking for the Rust toolchain'
    $cargo = Get-Command 'cargo.exe' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $rustup = Get-Command 'rustup.exe' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $cargo -or -not $rustup) {
        throw 'Rust was not found. Install the stable Rust toolchain from https://rustup.rs, then close and reopen your terminal.'
    }
    Write-Ok "cargo: $($cargo.Source)"
    Write-Ok "rustup: $($rustup.Source)"

    Write-Step "Verifying target $Target"
    $targetList = & $rustup.Source target list --installed
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "rustup could not list installed targets (exit code $LASTEXITCODE). Run 'rustup toolchain install stable' and try again."
    }
    if ($targetList -notcontains $Target) {
        Write-Warn "Installing missing Rust target $Target"
        & $rustup.Source target add $Target
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            throw "Could not install Rust target $Target (exit code $LASTEXITCODE)."
        }
    }
    Write-Ok "$Target available"

    Write-Step 'Checking for the Visual C++ build tools and Windows SDK'
    $programFilesX86 = ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($programFilesX86)) {
        $programFilesX86 = $env:ProgramFiles
    }
    $vswhere = Join-Path $programFilesX86 'Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe'
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $vswhere)) {
        throw 'Visual Studio Build Tools were not found. Install Visual Studio Build Tools with the "Desktop development with C++" workload and a Windows 10/11 SDK.'
    }

    $vsInstallPath = & $vswhere -latest -products '*' -requires 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64' -property installationPath 2>$null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace(($vsInstallPath | Select-Object -First 1))) {
        throw 'The MSVC C++ compiler tools were not found. Open Visual Studio Installer, modify your installation, and add the "Desktop development with C++" workload.'
    }
    Write-Ok "MSVC installation: $(($vsInstallPath | Select-Object -First 1).Trim())"

    Write-Step 'Building release executable'
    Push-Location $Root
    try {
        $lockFile = Join-Path $Root 'Cargo.lock'
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $lockFile -PathType Leaf) {
            Write-Ok 'Cargo.lock found; Cargo will reuse its pinned versions and update the lockfile if the manifest requires it'
        } else {
            Write-Warn 'Cargo.lock is missing; Cargo will resolve dependencies and create it during this build.'
            Write-Warn 'Keep the generated Cargo.lock with the source project to make later builds reproducible.'
        }

        # Do not pass --locked here. It makes Cargo fail before compilation if
        # the checked-in lockfile does not match Cargo.toml (for example after
        # a dependency feature change). Normal `cargo build` still respects an
        # existing valid lockfile and updates it only when resolution requires it.
        $cargoArguments = @('build', '--release', '--workspace', '--target', $Target)
        & $cargo.Source @cargoArguments
        $cargoExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
        if ($cargoExitCode -ne 0) {
            throw "cargo build failed (exit code $cargoExitCode). The Cargo error above is the relevant failure; fix that issue and rerun this script."
        }
    } finally {
        Pop-Location
    }

    $targetDir = Join-Path $Root "target\$Target\release"
    $source = Join-Path $targetDir $BinName
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $source)) {
        throw "Build finished without producing the expected executable: $source"
    }

    Write-Step 'Checking executable architecture'
    function Get-PeArchitecture([string]$Path) {
        $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($Path)
        if ($bytes.Length -lt 0x40) { return 'unknown' }
        $peOffset = [BitConverter]::ToInt32($bytes, 0x3C)
        if ($peOffset -lt 0 -or ($peOffset + 6) -gt $bytes.Length) { return 'unknown' }
        if ([BitConverter]::ToUInt32($bytes, $peOffset) -ne 0x00004550) { return 'unknown' }
        $machine = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($bytes, $peOffset + 4)
        switch ($machine) {
            0x8664 { return 'x64' }
            0x014C { return 'x86' }
            default { return 'other' }
        }
    }

    $architecture = Get-PeArchitecture -Path $source
    if ($architecture -ne 'x64') {
        throw "$BinName has architecture '$architecture'; expected x64."
    }
    Write-Ok "$BinName : x64"

    Write-Step 'Staging release files'
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Dist)) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Dist -Force | Out-Null
    }

    # Remove obsolete artifacts from older builds that packaged a Steam hook.
    foreach ($stale in @('dwmapi.dll', 'winhttp.dll', 'locomotive_hook.dll')) {
        $path = Join-Path $Dist $stale
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $path) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $path -Force
            Write-Warn "Removed stale dist\$stale"
        }
    }
    $staleHookDir = Join-Path $Dist 'steamhook'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $staleHookDir) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $staleHookDir -Recurse -Force
        Write-Warn 'Removed stale dist\steamhook directory'
    }

    if ($Mode -eq 'standalone') {
        Copy-Item -LiteralPath $source -Destination (Join-Path $Dist $BinName) -Force
        Write-Ok "Wrote $BinName to $Dist"
    } else {
        $bundle = Join-Path $Dist 'locomotive'
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $bundle) {
            Remove-Item -LiteralPath $bundle -Recurse -Force
        }
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $bundle -Force | Out-Null
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Join-Path $bundle 'assets') -Force | Out-Null
        Copy-Item -LiteralPath $source -Destination (Join-Path $bundle $BinName) -Force

        foreach ($document in @('README.md', 'CHANGELOG.txt', 'LICENSE')) {
            $documentPath = Join-Path $Root "docs\$document"
            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $documentPath) {
                Copy-Item -LiteralPath $documentPath -Destination $bundle -Force
            }
        }
        foreach ($asset in @('icon.png', 'icon.ico')) {
            $assetPath = Join-Path $Root "assets\$asset"
            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $assetPath) {
                Copy-Item -LiteralPath $assetPath -Destination (Join-Path $bundle 'assets') -Force
            }
        }
        Write-Ok "Wrote portable bundle to $bundle"
    }

    Write-Host ''
    Write-Host 'Build complete.' -ForegroundColor Green
    $ExitCode = 0
} catch {
    Write-Host ''
    Write-Fail $_.Exception.Message
    Write-Host 'See BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md for prerequisites and troubleshooting.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
} finally {
    if ($ExitCode -ne 0) {
        Write-Host ''
        Write-Host 'Build failed.' -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

exit $ExitCode


===== FILE: scripts\get_codebase.bat =====
@echo off
setlocal
REM ============================================================
REM  dump.bat [root_dir] [output_file]
REM  Example:  dump.bat C:\projects\myapp dump.txt
REM  Defaults: root = current dir, output = codebase_dump.txt
REM ============================================================

set "ROOT=%~1"
if "%ROOT%"=="" set "ROOT=%~dp0.."
set "OUT=%~2"
if "%OUT%"=="" set "OUT=%CD%\codebase_dump.txt"

echo Dumping: %ROOT%
echo Output : %OUT%
echo.

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ^
  "$ErrorActionPreference='SilentlyContinue';" ^
  "$root='%ROOT%'; $out='%OUT%';" ^
  "$skipDirs='\\\.git\\|\\node_modules\\|\\bin\\|\\obj\\|\\\.vs\\|\\dist\\|\\build\\|\\\.next\\|\\__pycache__\\|\\\.venv\\|\\venv\\|\\\.idea\\|\\\.vscode\\|\\coverage\\|\\target\\|\\out\\|\\Detours\\';" ^
  "$skipExt='\.(exe|dll|pdb|so|dylib|class|jar|pyc|o|a|lib|bin|zip|tar|gz|7z|rar|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|bmp|ico|pdf|mp3|mp4|avi|mov|wav|flac|woff|woff2|ttf|eot|otf|db|sqlite|lock|map|min\.js)$';" ^
  "if(Test-Path $out){Remove-Item $out -Force};" ^
  "$files = Get-ChildItem -Path $root -Recurse -File -Force | Where-Object { $p=$_.FullName; -not ($p -match $skipDirs) -and -not ($p -match $skipExt) } | Sort-Object FullName;" ^
  "'===== CODEBASE DUMP =====' | Set-Content $out;" ^
  "('Root : '+$root)  | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "('Date : '+(Get-Date)) | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "('Files: '+$files.Count) | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "'' | Add-Content $out;" ^
  "foreach($f in $files){" ^
  "  $rel = $f.FullName.Substring($root.Length).TrimStart('\');" ^
  "  Add-Content $out '';" ^
  "  Add-Content $out ('===== FILE: '+$rel+' =====');" ^
  "  try { Add-Content $out -Value (Get-Content -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Raw -ErrorAction Stop) }" ^
  "  catch { Add-Content $out '[unreadable / binary]' }" ^
  "};" ^
  "Write-Host ('Done. '+$files.Count+' files written to '+$out)"

endlocal
pause

===== FILE: src\app.rs =====
//! Application construction: boot function, window settings, and the
//! one-time wiring of the update/view/subscription functions into Iced.

use iced::window::{self, settings::platform::CornerPreference};
use iced::{Font, Size};

use crate::state::State;
use crate::theme;
use crate::update;
use crate::views;

/// The user-facing application name. Used in the titlebar and About panel.
pub const APP_NAME: &str = "Locomotive";

/// The user-facing version string. Shown in the About panel.
pub const APP_VERSION: &str = "0.0.1 Alpha";

/// Builds and runs the application.
pub fn run() -> iced::Result {
    iced::application(State::default, update::handle, views::root)
        .title(APP_NAME)
        .theme(theme_for)
        .default_font(Font::with_name("Fira Sans"))
        .font(lucide_icons::LUCIDE_FONT_BYTES)
        .subscription(State::subscription)
        .window(window::Settings {
            decorations: false,
            transparent: false,
            resizable: true,
            minimizable: true,
            closeable: true,
            size: Size::new(760.0, 520.0),
            min_size: Some(Size::new(640.0, 440.0)),
            platform_specific: windows_platform(),
            ..window::Settings::default()
        })
        .run()
}

fn theme_for(_state: &State) -> iced::Theme {
    theme::app_theme()
}

fn windows_platform() -> window::settings::PlatformSpecific {
    window::settings::PlatformSpecific {
        corner_preference: CornerPreference::Round,
        ..Default::default()
    }
}

===== FILE: src\assets.rs =====
//! Brand asset loading.
//!
//! The SVG is loaded from `assets/icon.svg` at compile time and its handle
//! is cached in a `OnceLock`. Every call to `brand_handle` returns a cheap
//! clone of the same handle, which keeps the renderer's cache key stable.
//!
//! Building a fresh handle per `view()` call would give the renderer a new
//! cache key per frame, and the SVG would be re-rasterized continuously.
//! That is the same failure mode that previously pushed idle memory from
//! 6 MB to over 20 MB with the image widget.

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use iced::widget::svg;

static BRAND_HANDLE: OnceLock<svg::Handle> = OnceLock::new();

/// The titlebar brand mark handle. Built once, cached, and cloned cheaply.
pub fn brand_handle() -> svg::Handle {
    BRAND_HANDLE
        .get_or_init(|| {
            let bytes: &'static [u8] = include_bytes!("../assets/icon.svg");
            svg::Handle::from_memory(bytes)
        })
        .clone()
}

===== FILE: src\backend\archive.rs =====
//! Default local storage and validation for the two import destinations.
//!
//! By default, imports go directly into Steam's active directories:
//!   .lua files      -> <Steam>\config\stplug-in
//!   .manifest files -> <Steam>\depotcache
//!
//! Those two directories are the ones Steam's own client, and BetterSteamTools,
//! read at start-up. Writing to them is the whole point of the tool.
//!
//! If no Steam installation is discovered, the tool falls back to a private
//! local library under the user's application data folder so the UI still
//! works on machines without Steam.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};

use super::steam;

/// The two independent import destinations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct StorageSettings {
    /// Folder used for `.manifest` and `.manifests` files.
    pub manifest_dir: PathBuf,
    /// Folder used for `.lua` files.
    pub lua_dir: PathBuf,
}

/// Returns the default destinations. Prefers Steam's active directories
/// when a Steam installation is present; otherwise uses a private local
/// library so the application remains usable.
pub(crate) fn default_settings() -> StorageSettings {
    if let Some(root) = steam::discover_root() {
        return StorageSettings {
            manifest_dir: steam::depotcache_dir(&root),
            lua_dir: steam::stplug_in_dir(&root),
        };
    }

    let root = data_directory().join("Locomotive").join("library");
    StorageSettings {
        manifest_dir: root.join("manifests"),
        lua_dir: root.join("lua"),
    }
}

/// Loads saved locations, falling back to the current defaults on invalid data.
pub(crate) fn load_settings() -> StorageSettings {
    let defaults = default_settings();
    let Ok(contents) = fs::read_to_string(settings_file()) else {
        return defaults;
    };

    let mut manifest_dir = None;
    let mut lua_dir = None;
    for line in contents.lines() {
        if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix("manifest=") {
            manifest_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
        } else if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix("lua=") {
            lua_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
        }
    }

    let Some(manifest_dir) = manifest_dir else {
        return defaults;
    };
    let Some(lua_dir) = lua_dir else {
        return defaults;
    };
    match normalize_and_validate(manifest_dir, lua_dir) {
        Ok(settings) => settings,
        Err(_) => defaults,
    }
}

/// Validates and persists the two import destinations.
pub(crate) fn save_settings(
    manifest_dir: &Path,
    lua_dir: &Path,
) -> Result<StorageSettings, String> {
    let settings = normalize_and_validate(manifest_dir.to_path_buf(), lua_dir.to_path_buf())?;
    fs::create_dir_all(&settings.manifest_dir).map_err(|error| {
        format!("Could not create manifest folder '{}': {error}", settings.manifest_dir.display())
    })?;
    fs::create_dir_all(&settings.lua_dir).map_err(|error| {
        format!("Could not create Lua folder '{}': {error}", settings.lua_dir.display())
    })?;

    let file = settings_file();
    if let Some(parent) = file.parent() {
        fs::create_dir_all(parent)
            .map_err(|error| format!("Could not create settings folder '{}': {error}", parent.display()))?;
    }
    let contents = format!(
        "manifest={}\nlua={}\n",
        settings.manifest_dir.display(),
        settings.lua_dir.display()
    );
    fs::write(&file, contents)
        .map_err(|error| format!("Could not save storage settings '{}': {error}", file.display()))?;

    Ok(settings)
}

/// Returns a settings-independent pair of normalized paths, rejecting
/// unsafe overlaps and paths inside a Steam installation that are not
/// one of the two active directories the tool is designed to write to.
pub(crate) fn normalize_and_validate(
    manifest_dir: PathBuf,
    lua_dir: PathBuf,
) -> Result<StorageSettings, String> {
    let manifest_dir = resolve_existing_prefix(&manifest_dir)?;
    let lua_dir = resolve_existing_prefix(&lua_dir)?;

    if same_or_nested(&manifest_dir, &lua_dir) || same_or_nested(&lua_dir, &manifest_dir) {
        return Err("Manifest and Lua folders must be separate and must not contain one another.".into());
    }
    for path in [&manifest_dir, &lua_dir] {
        if is_rejected_steam_path(path) {
            return Err(format!(
                "'{}' is inside a Steam installation but is not one of the two folders the tool writes to. Use <Steam>\\depotcache for manifests and <Steam>\\config\\stplug-in for Lua files, or pick a folder outside Steam.",
                path.display()
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(StorageSettings { manifest_dir, lua_dir })
}

fn absolute_normalized(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let absolute = if path.is_absolute() {
        path.to_path_buf()
    } else {
        std::env::current_dir()
            .map_err(|error| format!("Could not resolve relative path '{}': {error}", path.display()))?
            .join(path)
    };
    let mut normalized = PathBuf::new();
    for component in absolute.components() {
        match component {
            Component::CurDir => {}
            Component::ParentDir => {
                normalized.pop();
            }
            other => normalized.push(other.as_os_str()),
        }
    }
    Ok(normalized)
}

/// Resolves existing symlinked ancestors before validating a destination. The final
/// directory does not need to exist yet; any missing suffix is appended after the
/// nearest existing ancestor has been canonicalized.
fn resolve_existing_prefix(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let normalized = absolute_normalized(path)?;
    let mut existing = normalized.as_path();
    let mut missing = Vec::new();

    while !existing.exists() {
        let name = existing.file_name().ok_or_else(|| {
            format!("Could not resolve storage directory '{}'.", normalized.display())
        })?;
        missing.push(name.to_os_string());
        existing = existing.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
            format!("Could not resolve storage directory '{}'.", normalized.display())
        })?;
    }

    let mut resolved = fs::canonicalize(existing).map_err(|error| {
        format!("Could not resolve existing path '{}': {error}", existing.display())
    })?;
    for component in missing.iter().rev() {
        resolved.push(component);
    }
    absolute_normalized(&resolved)
}

fn same_or_nested(path: &Path, parent: &Path) -> bool {
    if cfg!(windows) {
        let path = path.to_string_lossy().trim_end_matches(|ch| ch == '\\' || ch == '/').to_lowercase();
        let parent = parent.to_string_lossy().trim_end_matches(|ch| ch == '\\' || ch == '/').to_lowercase();
        path == parent || path.starts_with(&format!("{parent}\\")) || path.starts_with(&format!("{parent}/"))
    } else {
        path == parent || path.starts_with(parent)
    }
}

/// True if `path` is exactly the stplug-in directory or a subdirectory of it.
fn is_stplug_in(path: &Path) -> bool {
    let components: Vec<String> = path
        .components()
        .map(|component| component.as_os_str().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    components.windows(2).any(|pair| {
        pair[0].eq_ignore_ascii_case("config") && pair[1].eq_ignore_ascii_case("stplug-in")
    })
}

/// True if `path` is exactly a directory named `depotcache` or a subdirectory of one.
fn is_depotcache(path: &Path) -> bool {
    path.components().any(|component| {
        component.as_os_str().to_string_lossy().eq_ignore_ascii_case("depotcache")
    })
}

/// True when the path is inside a Steam installation but is not one of the
/// two active directories the tool is designed to write to.
fn is_rejected_steam_path(path: &Path) -> bool {
    if is_stplug_in(path) || is_depotcache(path) {
        return false;
    }
    // Block writing directly inside steamapps (protects game files)
    // but allow custom folders elsewhere in the Steam directory (e.g. config/lua).
    path.ancestors().any(|ancestor| {
        ancestor.join("steamapps").is_dir() && ancestor.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) == Some("steamapps")
    })
}

fn settings_file() -> PathBuf {
    config_directory().join("Locomotive").join("paths.conf")
}

fn data_directory() -> PathBuf {
    #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
    if let Some(path) = std::env::var_os("LOCALAPPDATA") {
        return PathBuf::from(path);
    }
    std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."))
}


/// Returns the private cache directory used for game names and cover art.
pub(crate) fn cache_directory() -> PathBuf {
    data_directory().join("Locomotive").join("cache")
}

fn config_directory() -> PathBuf {
    #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
    if let Some(path) = std::env::var_os("APPDATA") {
        return PathBuf::from(path);
    }
    std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::path::PathBuf;

    use super::normalize_and_validate;

    #[test]
    fn storage_directories_must_not_overlap() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join("locomotive-storage-validation");
        let result = normalize_and_validate(root.join("files"), root.join("files/lua"));
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn independent_directories_are_accepted_outside_steam() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join("locomotive-storage-validation");
        let result = normalize_and_validate(root.join("manifests"), root.join("lua"));
        assert!(result.is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalizes_relative_path_components() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir();
        let result = normalize_and_validate(
            root.join("locomotive-normalize/../manifests"),
            root.join("locomotive-normalize/lua"),
        );
        assert!(result.is_ok());
        let settings = result.expect("the normalized paths should be independent");
        assert_eq!(settings.manifest_dir, root.join("manifests"));
        assert_eq!(settings.lua_dir, root.join("locomotive-normalize/lua"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_two_steam_active_directories_are_accepted() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("locomotive-steam-path-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let steamapps = root.join("steamapps");
        let config = root.join("config");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&steamapps).expect("test steamapps directory should be created");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&config).expect("test config directory should be created");
        let result = normalize_and_validate(
            root.join("depotcache"),
            config.join("stplug-in"),
        );
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        assert!(result.is_ok(), "the tool's two active directories must be permitted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn other_paths_inside_a_steam_installation_are_rejected() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("locomotive-steam-reject-test-{}", std::process::id()));
        let steamapps = root.join("steamapps");
        let config = root.join("config");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&steamapps).expect("test steamapps directory should be created");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&config).expect("test config directory should be created");
        let result = normalize_and_validate(
            steamapps.join("common").join("SomeGame"),
            config.join("backup"),
        );
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        assert!(result.is_err(), "arbitrary paths inside Steam must still be rejected");
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_manifest_extension_aliases() {
        use crate::state::FileKind;
        assert_eq!(FileKind::from_path(&PathBuf::from("42.manifests")), FileKind::Manifest);
        assert_eq!(FileKind::from_path(&PathBuf::from("42.MANIFEST")), FileKind::Manifest);
    }
}

===== FILE: src\backend\artwork.rs =====
//! Cached Steam metadata and artwork enrichment for app-ID-based library entries.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::state::library_state::LibrarySnapshot;

use super::{archive, artwork_remote, steam};

const MAX_PARALLEL_LOOKUPS: usize = 8;

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Lookup {
    entry_index: usize,
    app_id: String,
    needs_name: bool,
    needs_cover: bool,
    cover_path: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// Attaches local Steam artwork and cached names without network access.
pub(crate) fn enrich_local(snapshot: &mut LibrarySnapshot) {
    let _ = prepare_lookups(snapshot);
    sort_by_name(snapshot);
}

/// Fills remaining names and covers through cached, background-friendly Steam lookups.
pub(crate) fn enrich_remote(snapshot: &mut LibrarySnapshot) {
    let Some((cache_dir, steam_root, lookups)) = prepare_lookups(snapshot) else {
        return;
    };

    for batch in lookups.chunks(MAX_PARALLEL_LOOKUPS) {
        let resolved = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            let handles: Vec<_> = batch
                .iter()
                .cloned()
                .map(|lookup| {
                    let cache_dir = &cache_dir;
                    let steam_root = steam_root.as_deref();
                    scope.spawn(move || resolve_lookup(lookup, cache_dir, steam_root))
                })
                .collect();
            handles
                .into_iter()
                .filter_map(|handle| handle.join().ok())
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        });

        for (entry_index, name, cover_path) in resolved {
            let Some(entry) = snapshot.entries.get_mut(entry_index) else {
                continue;
            };
            if let Some(name) = name {
                entry.name = name;
                entry.name_is_fallback = false;
            }
            if cover_path.is_some() {
                entry.cover_path = cover_path;
            }
        }
    }

    sort_by_name(snapshot);
}

fn prepare_lookups(
    snapshot: &mut LibrarySnapshot,
) -> Option<(PathBuf, Option<PathBuf>, Vec<Lookup>)> {
    if snapshot.entries.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    let cache_dir = archive::cache_directory();
    fs::create_dir_all(&cache_dir).ok()?;
    let steam_root = steam::discover_root();
    let mut lookups = Vec::new();

    for (entry_index, entry) in snapshot.entries.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        let Some(app_id) = entry.key.strip_prefix("app:") else {
            continue;
        };
        if app_id.is_empty() || !app_id.chars().all(|character| character.is_ascii_digit()) {
            continue;
        }

        if entry.name_is_fallback || entry.name == format!("App {app_id}") {
            if let Some(name) = read_cached_name(&cache_dir, app_id) {
                entry.name = name;
                entry.name_is_fallback = false;
            }
        }

        let local_cover = find_cover(steam_root.as_deref(), app_id);
        let cached_portrait = cached_portrait(&cache_dir, app_id);
        let cached_fallback = cached_header(&cache_dir, app_id);
        let cover_path = cached_portrait
            .or_else(|| local_cover.clone().filter(|path| !is_header_art(path)))
            .or(local_cover)
            .or(cached_fallback);
        let needs_name = entry.name_is_fallback || entry.name == format!("App {app_id}");
        // A cached wide banner is only a fallback, not a finished cover lookup:
        // keep trying for the portrait capsule on subsequent launches.
        let needs_cover = cover_path.as_deref().is_none_or(is_header_art);
        entry.cover_path = cover_path.clone();
        if needs_name || needs_cover {
            lookups.push(Lookup {
                entry_index,
                app_id: app_id.to_owned(),
                needs_name,
                needs_cover,
                cover_path,
            });
        }
    }

    Some((cache_dir, steam_root, lookups))
}

fn resolve_lookup(
    lookup: Lookup,
    cache_dir: &Path,
    steam_root: Option<&Path>,
) -> (usize, Option<String>, Option<PathBuf>) {
    let fetch_name = lookup.needs_name
        && !recent_failure(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id, "name", Duration::from_secs(6 * 60 * 60));
    let fetch_cover = lookup.needs_cover
        && !recent_failure(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id, "cover", Duration::from_secs(24 * 60 * 60));
    let metadata = (fetch_name || fetch_cover)
        .then(|| artwork_remote::fetch_app_metadata(&lookup.app_id))
        .flatten();

    let name = if lookup.needs_name {
        let resolved = metadata.as_ref().and_then(|metadata| metadata.name.clone());
        let resolved = resolved.or_else(|| read_cached_name(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id));
        let marker = failure_marker(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id, "name");
        if let Some(name) = &resolved {
            let _ = fs::write(cache_dir.join(format!("{}.name", lookup.app_id)), name);
            let _ = fs::remove_file(marker);
        } else if fetch_name {
            let _ = fs::write(marker, b"");
        }
        resolved
    } else {
        None
    };

    let downloaded_cover = if fetch_cover {
        artwork_remote::download_cover(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id, metadata.as_ref())
    } else {
        None
    };

    if fetch_cover {
        let marker = failure_marker(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id, "cover");
        if downloaded_cover.is_some() {
            let _ = fs::remove_file(marker);
        } else {
            let _ = fs::write(marker, b"");
        }
    }

    // Prefer a newly downloaded portrait over an older cached header banner.
    let cover_path = downloaded_cover
        .or(lookup.cover_path)
        .or_else(|| cached_cover(cache_dir, &lookup.app_id))
        .or_else(|| find_cover(steam_root, &lookup.app_id));
    (lookup.entry_index, name, cover_path)
}

fn recent_failure(cache_dir: &Path, app_id: &str, kind: &str, retry_after: Duration) -> bool {
    let Ok(metadata) = fs::metadata(failure_marker(cache_dir, app_id, kind)) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Ok(modified) = metadata.modified() else {
        return false;
    };
    modified.elapsed().is_ok_and(|elapsed| elapsed < retry_after)
}

fn failure_marker(cache_dir: &Path, app_id: &str, kind: &str) -> PathBuf {
    // Versioned markers bypass misses from earlier CDN strategies. v4 retries
    // App IDs whose older lookups could not find portrait or hashed CDN assets.
    cache_dir.join(format!("{app_id}.{kind}-v4-miss"))
}

fn read_cached_name(cache_dir: &Path, app_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let name = fs::read_to_string(cache_dir.join(format!("{app_id}.name"))).ok()?;
    let name = name.trim();
    (!name.is_empty() && name.len() < 512).then(|| name.to_owned())
}

fn cached_portrait(cache_dir: &Path, app_id: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    [
        cache_dir.join(format!("{app_id}.cover.jpg")),
        cache_dir.join(format!("{app_id}.cover.png")),
        cache_dir.join(format!("{app_id}.cover.jpeg")),
        cache_dir.join(format!("{app_id}.jpg")),
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .find(|path| artwork_remote::is_valid_cached_image(path))
}

fn cached_header(cache_dir: &Path, app_id: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    [
